questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the series of reactions given and identify the final product [Z].
questions.solution:
The starting material is 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Treatment with 20% $H_3PO_4$ causes acid-catalyzed dehydration to form 2-methylpropene [W].

$(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{H^+} (CH_3)_2C=CH_2$

Next, 2-methylpropene [W] undergoes hydroboration-oxidation with $(BH_3)_2$ in THF followed by $H_2O_2 / NaOH$. This results in the anti-Markovnikov addition of water, yielding the primary alcohol 2-methylpropan-1-ol [X].

$(CH_3)_2C=CH_2 \xrightarrow{(i) (BH_3)_2, (ii) H_2O_2/OH^-} (CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-OH$

Oxidation of the primary alcohol 2-methylpropan-1-ol [X] with $CrO_3$ yields the corresponding aldehyde, 2-methylpropanal [Y].

$(CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-OH \xrightarrow{CrO_3} (CH_3)_2CH-CHO$

Finally, 2-methylpropanal [Y] reacts with the Grignard reagent methylmagnesium bromide ($CH_3MgBr$) followed by hydrolysis to form the secondary alcohol 3-methylbutan-2-ol [Z].

$(CH_3)_2CH-CHO \xrightarrow{(i) CH_3MgBr, (ii) H_2O} (CH_3)_2CH-CH(OH)-CH_3$

The structure of 3-methylbutan-2-ol corresponds to the fourth option.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unsaturated organic compound (C_3$H_6$), undergoes the following series of reactions:
$\text{C}_3\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\large{dil\ H_2SO_4}} [\text{B}]\ (\text{Major Product}) \xrightarrow{\large{+\ HCl\ /\ ZnCl_2}} [\text{C}] \xrightarrow{\large{Na_{(s)}\ /\ dry\ ether}} [\text{D}]$
Identify compound [D]
questions.solution:
The unsaturated organic compound $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ is propene, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$.

Hydration of propene with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ follows Markovnikov's rule to give propan-2-ol as the major product [B].
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$

Reaction of propan-2-ol with Lucas reagent ($\text{HCl} / \text{ZnCl}_2$) gives 2-chloropropane [C].
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{HCl} / \text{ZnCl}_2} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CH}_3$

Wurtz reaction of 2-chloropropane with sodium in dry ether gives 2,3-dimethylbutane [D].
$2\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Na} / \text{dry ether}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$

Compound [D] is 2,3-dimethylbutane.

Answer: 2,3–dimethylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements [A] and [B] are given below. Choose the correct option.
A) Protonated R$-$CH_2-$OH can serve as Electrophiles while neutral R$-$OH acts as a Nucleophile. \\ B) The bond between O$-$H cleaves when R$-$CH_2-$OH acts as Electrophiles and the bond between C$-$O cleaves when they act as Nucleophiles.
options: Both the statements [A] and [B] are wrong
Statement [A] is correct but [B] is wrong
Both the statements [A] and [B] are correct
Statement [B] is correct but [A] is wrong
questions.solution:
Alcohols can act as both nucleophiles and electrophiles.

Neutral alcohols act as nucleophiles due to the presence of lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom. In these reactions, the O$-$H bond is cleaved.

Protonated alcohols act as electrophiles because protonation makes the hydroxyl group a good leaving group (H_2$O). In these reactions, a nucleophile attacks the carbon atom, and the C$-$O bond is cleaved. \\ \\ Statement [A] is correct as protonated R$-$CH_2-$OH acts as an electrophile and neutral R$-$OH acts as a nucleophile.

Statement [B] is incorrect because the C$-$O bond cleaves when alcohols act as electrophiles, and the O$-$H bond cleaves when they act as nucleophiles.

Answer: Statement [A] is correct but [B] is wrong

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Reaction of alcohols with anhydrides is carried out in the presence of small amounts of Conc. H_2$SO_4$ to remove the water formed
Relative ease of dehydration of alcohols on heating with a protic acid is Primary > Secondary > Tertiary
p– Nitrophenol is more acidic than p– Cresol
Cyclic C_4$H_7$OH exists as four structural isomers
questions.solution:
The relative ease of dehydration of alcohols on heating with a protic acid follows the order: Tertiary > Secondary > Primary. This is because the dehydration mechanism involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate, and the stability of carbocations follows the order $3^{\circ} \gt 2^{\circ} \gt 1^{\circ}$. Therefore, the given statement regarding the ease of dehydration is incorrect.

The reaction of alcohols with carboxylic acids and acid anhydrides is carried out in the presence of a small amount of concentrated $H_2SO_4$. The reaction is reversible, and the removal of water drives the equilibrium forward, making the first statement contextually accepted as per standard textbook language.

In p-nitrophenol, the $-NO_2$ group is strongly electron-withdrawing ($-M$ and $-I$ effects), which stabilizes the conjugate base and increases acidity. In p-cresol, the $-CH_3$ group is electron-donating ($+I$ and hyperconjugation), which destabilizes the conjugate base. Hence, p-nitrophenol is more acidic than p-cresol.

The formula $C_4H_7OH$ has a degree of unsaturation of $1$. The possible cyclic structural isomers are cyclobutanol, 1-methylcyclopropan-1-ol, 2-methylcyclopropan-1-ol, and cyclopropylmethanol. This gives exactly four structural isomers.

Answer: Relative ease of dehydration of alcohols on heating with a protic acid is Primary > Secondary > Tertiary

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound [X] undergoes reactions as given. Identify compounds [C] and [D] formed in these reactions.
questions.solution:
The given starting compound is isopropyl phenyl ether, $Ph-O-CH(CH_3)_2$.

Reaction with concentrated HI leads to the cleavage of the ether. Due to the partial double bond character of the O-phenyl bond (arising from resonance), the cleavage occurs at the O-isopropyl bond. This yields phenol and isopropyl iodide.
$Ph-O-CH(CH_3)_2 + HI \rightarrow PhOH + CH_3-CH(I)-CH_3$
Since [A] is the aromatic product, [A] is Phenol and [B] is Isopropyl iodide.

Phenol [A] undergoes oxidation with acidified dichromate ($Cr_2O_7^{2-} / H^+$) to form p-benzoquinone.
Therefore, [C] is Benzoquinone.

Isopropyl iodide [B] reacts with aqueous KOH to undergo nucleophilic substitution, forming isopropyl alcohol.
$CH_3-CH(I)-CH_3 + aq. KOH \rightarrow CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3$

Isopropyl alcohol contains the $CH_3-CH(OH)-$ group, which gives a positive iodoform test when treated with $I_2$ and a base like $Na_2CO_3$. The reaction produces iodoform and the sodium salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid (sodium acetate).
$CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3 + I_2 + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow CHI_3 + CH_3COONa$
Therefore, [D] is Iodoform.

Answer: [C]: Benzoquinone [D]: Iodoform

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Choose the correct reason:
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde is a liquid at room temperature while $p$-hydroxy-benzaldehyde is a high melting solid, because
options: p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in o-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonding
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows association of the molecules while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no association among the molecules
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows only weak Vanderwal's forces of attraction while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is strong Vanderwal's forces of attraction in solid state
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no intramolecular hydrogen bonding
questions.solution:
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding due to the proximity of the -OH and -CHO groups. This restricts the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, resulting in weaker intermolecular forces and making it a liquid at room temperature.

In p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, the -OH and -CHO groups are far apart, so it cannot form intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Instead, it forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds, leading to molecular association and a high melting point, making it a solid.

Thus, o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while p-hydroxybenzaldehyde does not.

Answer: o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no intramolecular hydrogen bonding

questions.solution:
Reaction A: Warming benzene diazonium chloride with water yields phenol. Thus, A matches with R.

Reaction B: Bromination of phenol in a non-polar solvent like $CS_2$ at low temperature ($273$ K) yields monobromophenols, primarily p-bromophenol as the major product. Thus, B matches with P.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aliphatic compound [X], Molecular formula ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) can be prepared from Acetone and R– Mg–X. [X] with 20% Phosphoric acid gives an unsaturated compound $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$ [Y]. Compound [Y] is also obtained on heating [X] with Copper metal at 573K. [X] shows no reaction with PCC but on heating with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ it forms Acetone + $\text{CO}_2$ + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Compounds [X] and [Y] are -------------------- and --------------------
questions.solution:
Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) reacts with methylmagnesium halide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgX}$) followed by hydrolysis to form a tertiary alcohol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgX} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH}$

Thus, compound [X] is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, which has the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

Dehydration of [X] with 20% $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ or heating with Cu at 573 K yields 2-methylpropene [Y].

$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Tertiary alcohols do not undergo oxidation with PCC, hence [X] shows no reaction.

Vigorous oxidation of [X] with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ involves dehydration to [Y] followed by oxidative cleavage of the double bond to form acetone, $\text{CO}_2$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Therefore, [X] is 2-methylpropan-2-ol and [Y] is 2-methylpropene.

Answer: [X]: 2–Methylpropan–2–ol [Y]: 2–Methylpropene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: Anisole is prepared by reaction between Bromobenzene and Sodium methoxide
Tert. butyl methyl ether reacts with Conc. HI on heating to form 2–Iodo–2–methylpropane and Methanol by $S_N1$ mechanism
Isopropyl methyl ether reacts with Conc. HI to produce isopropyl alcohol and methyl iodide by $S_N2$ mechanism
Anisole reacts with Ethanoyl chloride / anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in $\text{CS}_2$ to form 4–Methoxyacetophenone in larger amount
questions.solution:
Bromobenzene does not undergo nucleophilic substitution easily due to the partial double bond character of the C-Br bond. Therefore, anisole cannot be prepared by the reaction between bromobenzene and sodium methoxide.

Anisole is prepared by Williamson ether synthesis using sodium phenoxide and methyl halide (such as methyl bromide or methyl iodide).

Tert-butyl methyl ether reacts with concentrated HI via an $S_N1$ mechanism because the tert-butyl carbocation is highly stable, yielding 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol.

Isopropyl methyl ether reacts with concentrated HI via an $S_N2$ mechanism where the iodide ion attacks the less sterically hindered methyl group, producing methyl iodide and isopropyl alcohol.

Anisole undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with ethanoyl chloride and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form 4-methoxyacetophenone as the major product due to the para-directing nature of the methoxy group and less steric hindrance at the para position.

Thus, the statement in option (A) is wrong.

Answer: Anisole is prepared by reaction between Bromobenzene and Sodium methoxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the most suitable method for the preparation of allylphenylether?
questions.solution:
The preparation of allyl phenyl ether involves the Williamson ether synthesis, which is a nucleophilic substitution reaction between an alkoxide or phenoxide ion and an alkyl halide.

The reaction requires a phenoxide ion (nucleophile) and an allyl halide (electrophile).

Option (2) shows the reaction between sodium phenoxide ($C_{6}H_{5}ONa$) and allyl bromide ($CH_{2}=CH-CH_{2}Br$). This is a classic $S_{N}2$ reaction where the phenoxide oxygen attacks the primary allylic carbon, displacing the bromide ion to form allyl phenyl ether ($C_{6}H_{5}-O-CH_{2}-CH=CH_{2}$).

Option (1) involves vinyl bromide, which is unreactive towards $S_{N}2$ substitution due to the partial double bond character of the $C-Br$ bond and the instability of the vinyl cation. Option (3) involves a vinyl halide and methoxide. Option (4) involves benzyl bromide and an allyl alkoxide, which would produce allyl benzyl ether, not allyl phenyl ether.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their acidic strength 4-chlorophenol (I), 4-methylphenol(II), 4-nitrophenol(III), 4-methoxyphenol(IV) and phenol(V)
questions.solution:
The acidic strength of substituted phenols depends on the electronic effects of the substituents attached to the benzene ring. Electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) increase acidity by stabilizing the phenoxide ion through inductive (-I) or resonance (-M) effects, while electron-donating groups (EDG) decrease acidity by destabilizing the phenoxide ion through inductive (+I) or resonance (+M) effects.

The substituents in the given compounds are:
I: 4-chlorophenol (Cl group, -I effect, +M effect; overall -I effect dominates, making it more acidic than phenol).
II: 4-methylphenol (C$H_{3}$ group, +I effect and hyperconjugation, making it less acidic than phenol). \\ III: 4-nitrophenol (NO_{2}$ group, strong -I and -M effects, making it the most acidic).
IV: 4-methoxyphenol (OCH_{3}$ group, +M effect dominates over -I effect, making it the least acidic). \\ V: Phenol (reference compound). \\ \\ Comparing the effects: \\ The -M effect of NO_{2}$ in III is very strong, making it the most acidic. The -I effect of Cl in I makes it more acidic than phenol. The +I and hyperconjugation of CH_{3}$ in II make it less acidic than phenol. The +M effect of OCH_{3}$ in IV is stronger than the +I effect of CH_{3}$, making IV the least acidic. \\ \\ The order of increasing acidic strength is: IV < II < V < I < III. \\ \\ Answer: IV < II < V < I < III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify X and Y formed in the following two reactions.
(i) Decan-1-ol $\xrightarrow{\text { Jones reagent }} \mathrm{X}$
(ii). Sodium salt of $\mathrm{X} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaOH} / \mathrm{CaO}, \Delta} \mathrm{Y}$
questions.solution:
Decan-1-ol is a primary alcohol with the formula $CH_{3}(CH_{2})_{8}CH_{2}OH$.

Jones reagent ($CrO_{3} / H_{2}SO_{4}$) is a strong oxidizing agent that oxidizes primary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids. Therefore, the oxidation of decan-1-ol yields decanoic acid ($CH_{3}(CH_{2})_{8}COOH$), which is X.

The reaction of the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with soda lime ($NaOH / CaO$) is known as decarboxylation. This process removes the carboxyl group as $Na_{2}CO_{3}$ and replaces it with a hydrogen atom, resulting in an alkane with one less carbon atom than the original acid.

Decanoic acid has 10 carbon atoms. The sodium salt of decanoic acid is sodium decanoate. Upon heating with soda lime, it undergoes decarboxylation to form nonane ($CH_{3}(CH_{2})_{7}CH_{3}$), which is Y.

Answer: $\mathrm{X}=$ Decanoic acid $\quad \mathrm{Y}=$ Nonane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is the major product formed when the given reaction occurs?
questions.solution:
The reaction involves the cleavage of an ether and the hydrohalogenation of an alkene with excess concentrated HI.

First, the ether linkage $Ar-O-CH_2CH_3$ is cleaved by HI. The oxygen atom is protonated, and the iodide ion attacks the less sterically hindered alkyl group ($CH_2CH_3$) via an $S_N2$ mechanism, resulting in the formation of a phenol ($Ar-OH$) and ethyl iodide ($CH_3CH_2I$).

Second, the alkene group $-CH=CH_2$ attached to the benzene ring undergoes electrophilic addition with HI. According to Markovnikov's rule, the proton ($H^+$) adds to the terminal carbon ($CH_2$) to form a more stable benzylic carbocation ($Ar-CH^{+}-CH_3$), which is stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring. Subsequently, the iodide ion ($I^-$) attacks this carbocation to form the product $Ar-CH(I)-CH_3$.

Combining these two processes, the final product is 4-(1-iodoethyl)phenol. This corresponds to the structure where the hydroxyl group is attached to the benzene ring and the 1-iodoethyl group is at the para position.

Answer:

questions.q:
Match the reaction in Column I with the major product formed given in Column II.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|} \hline & \text { Column I- Reaction/conditions } & & \text { Column II- Product } \\ \hline A & \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6 \xrightarrow[\substack{\text{(ii) NaOH} \\ \text{(iii) H^+}}]{\text{(i) Oleum}} & P & \text { Pentan-2-ol. } \\ \hline B & \text{Butanal } \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \mathrm{H}^+]{\text{(i) } \text{MeMgBr/ dry ether}} & Q & \text { 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid. } \\ \hline C & \text {2-Methylpropene } \xrightarrow[\text { (ii) } \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2 / \mathrm{NaOH}]{\text { (i) } \mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6} & R & \text { Phenol } \\ \hline D & \text{Phenol } \xrightarrow[\text { (ii) } \mathrm{CO}_2, 400 \mathrm{~K}, 7 \mathrm{~atm} .]{\text { (i) } \mathrm{NaOH}} & S & \text { 2-Methylpropan-1-0 I } \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Reaction A: Benzene reacts with oleum to form benzenesulfonic acid, which upon fusion with NaOH followed by acidification yields phenol. Thus, A = R.

Reaction B: Butanal ($CH_3CH_2CH_2CHO$) reacts with methylmagnesium bromide ($MeMgBr$) followed by acidic workup to form a secondary alcohol. Specifically, $CH_3CH_2CH_2CHO + CH_3MgBr \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH_2CH(OMgBr)CH_3 \xrightarrow{H^+} CH_3CH_2CH_2CH(OH)CH_3$, which is pentan-2-ol. Thus, B = P.

Reaction C: 2-Methylpropene ($CH_3C(CH_3)=CH_2$) undergoes hydroboration-oxidation. The reaction follows anti-Markovnikov addition of water, yielding 2-methylpropan-1-ol. Thus, C = S.

Reaction D: Phenol reacts with NaOH to form sodium phenoxide, which undergoes Kolbe-Schmitt reaction with $CO_2$ at high pressure and temperature to yield 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid). Thus, D = Q.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following compounds will give a yellow precipitate when reacted with $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{NaOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The iodoform test is given by compounds containing the $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CO}-$ group or the $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH(OH)}-$ group. These groups are oxidized to the methyl ketone group, which then reacts with $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{NaOH}$ to form a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\mathrm{CHI}_3$).

Analyzing the options:
1. $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$ is a primary alcohol and does not contain the required $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH(OH)}-$ structural unit.
2. $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3 \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}$ is a tertiary alcohol and cannot be oxidized to a methyl ketone.
3. $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$ (phenol) does not contain the $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH(OH)}-$ or $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CO}-$ group.
4. $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CHOH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ is a secondary alcohol containing the $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH(OH)}-$ group attached to a phenyl ring. Upon oxidation, it forms acetophenone ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{COCH}_3$), which contains the $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CO}-$ group and thus gives a positive iodoform test.

Answer: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CHOH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What are the intermediates formed during the reactions A and B ?
A. Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
B. Dehydration of alcohols in the slow rate determining step.
questions.solution:
A. Reimer-Tiemann Reaction:
Phenol is treated with $CHCl_3$ and $NaOH$. The base generates dichlorocarbene $(:CCl_2)$, which attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion. The intermediate is sodium 2-(dichloromethyl)phenolate — a phenoxide ring with an ortho $-CHCl_2$ group (option 4, structure A).

B. Dehydration of Alcohols (slow step):
In acid-catalyzed E1 dehydration, the slow rate-determining step is the breaking of the C$-$O bond after protonation of $-OH$, forming a carbocation $R^+$. The intermediate is the carbocation $H_3C-\overset{(+)}{C}-H$ (option 4, structure B).

Option (4) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: In the acid catalysed hydration of Ethene, an Oxonium ion is formed when it reacts with $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}$and a Carbocation is formed when the Oxonium ion reacts with water.
Cresols are less acidic than Phenol because electron releasing groups do not favour formation of Phenoxide ion.
Ethanol acts as Nucleophile when the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond is broken and acts as Electrophile on getting protonated.
In the reaction between Ethanol and Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ at 413 K , an Oxonium ion is formed when Ethanol gets protonated.
questions.solution:
In the acid catalysed hydration of ethene, the mechanism involves the protonation of ethene by $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^{+}$ to form a carbocation intermediate, not an oxonium ion. The water molecule then acts as a nucleophile to attack the carbocation. Thus, the statement in option (NCmIr) is incorrect.

Cresols contain a methyl group, which is an electron-donating group (+I effect). This destabilizes the phenoxide ion formed after the loss of a proton, making cresols less acidic than phenol. This statement is correct.

Ethanol acts as a nucleophile when the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond breaks (e.g., in esterification) and acts as an electrophile when the oxygen is protonated (e.g., in dehydration or substitution reactions where $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a leaving group). This statement is correct.

In the reaction between ethanol and concentrated $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ at 413 K, the first step is the protonation of the oxygen atom of ethanol to form an alkyloxonium ion, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}_2^{+}$. This statement is correct.

Answer: In the acid catalysed hydration of Ethene, an Oxonium ion is formed when it reacts with $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}$and a Carbocation is formed when the Oxonium ion reacts with water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify $[\mathrm{X}]$ used in the given reaction.
$[\mathrm{X}]+$ Copper $/ 573 \mathrm{~K} \rightarrow[\mathrm{Y}][\mathrm{Y}] \xrightarrow[\text { (ii) } \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / \mathrm{H}^{+}]{\text {(i) } \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{MgBr}}$ Tert.butyl alcohol. (major product)
questions.solution:
The reaction of $[\mathrm{Y}]$ with $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields tert-butyl alcohol, which is 2-methylpropan-2-ol. This indicates that $[\mathrm{Y}]$ must be acetone (propanone), as the Grignard reaction of acetone with methylmagnesium bromide produces tert-butyl alcohol.

The reaction $[\mathrm{X}] + \text{Copper} / 573 \mathrm{~K} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Y}]$ represents the dehydrogenation of an alcohol to a carbonyl compound. Since $[\mathrm{Y}]$ is propanone ($CH_3COCH_3$), $[\mathrm{X}]$ must be a secondary alcohol with three carbon atoms, which is propan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(OH)CH_3$).

The sequence is: Propan-2-ol $\xrightarrow{\text{Cu}, 573 \mathrm{K}}$ Propanone $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr}, \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{H}^{+}}$ 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

Answer: Propan-2-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, One Assertion [A ] and the other Reason [ R ] are given. Identify the correct option Assertion [A]: The decreasing order of the acidic character of the following is $\mathrm{B}\gt \mathrm{D}\gt \mathrm{A}\gt \mathrm{C}$
Reason $[\mathrm{R}]$ : Fluorine has larger -I effect than Cl and Br .
options: A is wrong but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A .
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$.
questions.solution:
The acidity of substituted cyclohexanols is determined by the inductive effect (-I effect) of the substituent. The -I effect increases the acidity of the hydroxyl group by stabilizing the conjugate base (alkoxide ion) through electron withdrawal.

The strength of the -I effect follows the order: F > Cl > Br. The methyl group (-C$H_{3}$) exhibits a +I effect, which destabilizes the conjugate base and decreases acidity compared to the unsubstituted cyclohexanol. \\ \\ Comparing the structures: \\ [A] 4-bromocyclohexanol: -I effect of Br. \\ [B] 2-chlorocyclohexanol: -I effect of Cl at the ortho position. \\ [C] 2-methylcyclohexanol: +I effect of CH_{3}$ at the ortho position.
[D] 4-fluorocyclohexanol: -I effect of F.

The -I effect is distance-dependent. Substituents at the 2-position (ortho) have a stronger effect than those at the 4-position (para). Thus, the order of acidity is determined by the strength of the -I effect and the proximity to the -OH group. The order is [B] (Cl at 2-position) > [D] (F at 4-position) > [A] (Br at 4-position) > [C] (CH_{3}$ at 2-position).

Assertion [A] states the order B > D > A > C, which is correct. Reason [R] states that Fluorine has a larger -I effect than Cl and Br, which is also correct. However, the reason for the order B > D is the proximity of the substituent (ortho vs para), not just the strength of the -I effect of the halogen itself. Therefore, R is not the correct explanation for A.

Answer: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following in the decreasing order of their $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ values.
questions.solution:
The acidity of phenols is determined by the stability of the phenoxide ion formed after the loss of a proton. Electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) increase acidity (lower $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$), while electron-donating groups (EDG) decrease acidity (higher $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$).

The substituents at the para position for the given compounds are:
[A] $-\text{NH}_{2}$: Strong electron-donating group by resonance ($+M$).
[B] $-\text{NO}_{2}$: Strong electron-withdrawing group by resonance ($-M$) and induction ($-I$).
[C] $-\text{OCH}_{3}$: Electron-donating group by resonance ($+M$) but electron-withdrawing by induction ($-I$). Overall, it acts as a weak electron donor.
[D] $-\text{Cl}$: Electron-withdrawing group by induction ($-I$) but electron-donating by resonance ($+M$). Overall, it acts as a weak electron withdrawer.

Comparing the electron-donating/withdrawing effects:
The $-\text{NH}_{2}$ group is the strongest electron donor, making [A] the least acidic (highest $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$).
The $-\text{OCH}_{3}$ group is a weaker electron donor than $-\text{NH}_{2}$, making [C] less acidic than [D] and [B] but more acidic than [A].
The $-\text{Cl}$ group is an electron withdrawer, making [D] more acidic than [A] and [C].
The $-\text{NO}_{2}$ group is the strongest electron withdrawer, making [B] the most acidic (lowest $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$).

The acidity order is $\text{B} \gt \text{D} \gt \text{C} \gt \text{A}$.
Since $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$ is inversely proportional to acidity, the decreasing order of $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$ values is $\text{A} \gt \text{C} \gt \text{D} \gt \text{B}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}\gt \mathrm{C}\gt \mathrm{D}\gt \mathrm{B}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of their acidic strength.
(I) m-cresol
(II) Phenol
(III) m-aminophenol
(IV) m-methoxyphenol
questions.solution:
At meta position, only inductive effect (I-effect) operates, not resonance.

m-methoxyphenol: $-OCH_3$ has strong $-I$ effect (O is highly electronegative) → stabilizes phenoxide → most acidic.

m-aminophenol: $-NH_2$ has $-I$ effect but weaker than $-OCH_3$ (N less electronegative than O) → more acidic than phenol.

Phenol: reference compound, no substituent.

m-cresol: $-CH_3$ has $+I$ effect → destabilizes phenoxide → least acidic.

Decreasing order: IV > III > II > I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compound cannot be prepared by Williamson's synthesis?
questions.solution:
Williamson synthesis involves the reaction of an alkoxide ion with an alkyl halide via an $S_{N}2$ mechanism. Since $S_{N}2$ reactions are highly sensitive to steric hindrance, the alkyl halide used must be primary for the reaction to proceed efficiently. If a tertiary alkyl halide is used, elimination (E2) becomes the dominant pathway, leading to the formation of an alkene instead of an ether.

In the case of $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{COC}\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3$ (di-tert-butyl ether), the synthesis would require the reaction of a tert-butoxide ion with a tert-butyl halide. Because the tert-butyl halide is a tertiary substrate, it undergoes rapid elimination to form isobutylene rather than substitution. Therefore, di-tert-butyl ether cannot be prepared by Williamson synthesis.

Answer: $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{COC}\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following tests may be used to distinguish between phenol and cyclohexanol?
questions.solution:
Phenol is an aromatic compound containing a hydroxyl group attached directly to a benzene ring, which imparts acidic character to the molecule. Cyclohexanol is an aliphatic cyclic alcohol.

The ferric chloride test is a characteristic test for phenols. Phenols react with neutral ferric chloride solution to form a violet, green, or blue colored complex, which is due to the formation of iron-phenolate complexes. Cyclohexanol, being an aliphatic alcohol, does not give this test.

The Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. The iodoform test is used to detect the presence of a methyl ketone group or a methyl carbinol group (C$H_3$CH(OH)-). Reaction with sodium metal is given by both phenols and alcohols due to the presence of the hydroxyl group, so it cannot distinguish between them.

Answer: Ferric chloride test

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product '$\mathrm{X}$' of the following reaction is
questions.solution:
The reaction is an acid-catalyzed dehydration of a secondary alcohol, 3,3-dimethylpentan-2-ol. The mechanism proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

Protonation of the hydroxyl group by $H_{2}SO_{4}$ to form a good leaving group, $-OH_{2}^{+}$.

Loss of water molecule to form a secondary carbocation at the C2 position: $CH_{3}-CH^{+}-C(CH_{3})_{2}-CH_{2}-CH_{3}$.

The secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation: $CH_{3}-CH(CH_{3})-C^{+}(CH_{3})-CH_{2}-CH_{3}$.

Elimination of a proton from the adjacent carbon to form the most stable alkene (Zaitsev product). The tertiary carbocation can lose a proton from the C2 position to form 2,3-dimethylpent-2-ene, which is a highly substituted and stable alkene.

Therefore, the major product is 2,3-dimethylpent-2-ene.

Answer: 2, 3-dimethylpent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, Assertion and Reason are given below. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: n-propyl tert-butyl ether can be readily prepared in the laboratory by Williamson's synthesis.
Reason: The reaction occurs by $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ attack of Primary alkoxide on Tert-alkyl halide to give good yield of the product, n-propyl tert-butyl ether.
options: Assertion is incorrect but reason is correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct: n-propyl tert-butyl ether can be prepared by Williamson synthesis by reacting sodium tert-butoxide (tertiary alkoxide) with 1-bromopropane (primary alkyl halide) via $S_N2$.

Reason is incorrect for two reasons: Williamson synthesis proceeds via $S_N2$, not $S_N1$. Also, if a primary alkoxide attacks a tert-alkyl halide, the strong base would cause E2 elimination (forming isobutylene) rather than substitution, giving very poor yield of the ether.

Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct order of reagents to be used to convent [A] to [X] ? $ \text { Reagents: } \mathrm{PCC}, \mathrm{PCl}_5, \mathrm{LiAlH}_4, \dfrac{\mathrm{KCN}}{\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}}$
questions.solution:
The goal is to convert $R-CH_2-OH$ to $R-CH_2-CHO$ (adding one carbon via chain extension).

$PCl_5$: Converts alcohol to alkyl chloride (good leaving group).
$R-CH_2-OH \xrightarrow{PCl_5} R-CH_2-Cl$

$KCN$: Nucleophilic substitution adds cyanide, extending the chain by one carbon.
$R-CH_2-Cl \xrightarrow{KCN} R-CH_2-CN$

$H_3O^+$: Acidic hydrolysis converts nitrile to carboxylic acid.
$R-CH_2-CN \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} R-CH_2-COOH$

$LiAlH_4$: Reduces carboxylic acid to primary alcohol.
$R-CH_2-COOH \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} R-CH_2-CH_2-OH$

$PCC$: Selectively oxidises primary alcohol to aldehyde (stops at aldehyde stage).
$R-CH_2-CH_2-OH \xrightarrow{PCC} R-CH_2-CHO$

Correct order: $PCl_5 \to \dfrac{KCN}{H_3O^+} \to LiAlH_4 \to PCC$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product $[\mathrm{D}]$ formed when Benzyl alcohol undergoes the following series of reactions
$\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow[\mathrm{A}]+\mathrm{KCN} \rightarrow[\mathrm{B}]+\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+} \text {(partial hydrolysis) } \rightarrow[\mathrm{C}]+\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+} \text {(complete hydrolysis) } \rightarrow[\mathrm{D}]$
questions.solution:
Benzyl alcohol is $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$.

Reaction with $\mathrm{SOCl}_2$ (Darzens process) converts the alcohol to an alkyl chloride: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{SO}_2 + \mathrm{HCl}$. Thus, $[\mathrm{A}]$ is Benzyl chloride ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl}$).

Reaction of $[\mathrm{A}]$ with $\mathrm{KCN}$ is a nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$): $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{KCN} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN} + \mathrm{KCl}$. Thus, $[\mathrm{B}]$ is Benzyl cyanide ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN}$).

Partial hydrolysis of $[\mathrm{B}]$ with $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}$ yields an amide: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN} + \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CONH}_2$. Thus, $[\mathrm{C}]$ is Phenylacetamide ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CONH}_2$).

Complete hydrolysis of $[\mathrm{C}]$ with $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}$ converts the amide group to a carboxylic acid group: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CONH}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_3$. Thus, $[\mathrm{D}]$ is 2-Phenylethanoic acid (also known as Phenylacetic acid).

Answer: 2-Phenylethanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
4 statements are given below. Identify the incorrect statement
A. Phenol has lower $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ value than $\mathrm{p}$-cresol
B. 2-Chlorophenol is more acidic than phenol
C. Ortho and para nitrophenols can be separated by steam distillation since $\mathrm{p}$-Nitrophenol is more steam volatile than o-Nitrophenol
D. Phenol on reaction with $\dfrac{\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}}{\mathrm{H}^{+}}$ yields a conjugated diketone
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct because the electron-donating methyl group in p-cresol decreases the acidity of the phenolic hydroxyl group compared to phenol, leading to a higher pKa value for p-cresol and a lower pKa value for phenol.

Statement B is correct because the electron-withdrawing chlorine atom in 2-chlorophenol stabilizes the phenoxide ion through the inductive effect, making it more acidic than phenol.

Statement C is incorrect. o-Nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which makes it more steam volatile. p-Nitrophenol exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which leads to higher association and lower steam volatility. Therefore, o-nitrophenol is the one that is steam volatile, not p-nitrophenol.

Statement D is correct because the oxidation of phenol with chromic acid ($\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}/\mathrm{H}^{+}$) yields p-benzoquinone, which is a conjugated diketone.

Answer: C

questions.q: Compounds $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$, having the same molecular formula $(\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_8 \mathrm{O})$, react separately with $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{MgBr}$, followed by reaction with dil. $\mathrm{HCl}$ to form compounds $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ respectively. Compound $\mathrm{Y}$ undergoes acidic dehydration in presence of Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ much more readily than $\mathrm{X}$. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the end-product [D] formed when solution salicylate undergoes the following series of reactions
questions.solution:
The starting material (A) is sodium salicylate. Treatment with NaOH/CaO/Heat is a decarboxylation reaction (soda-lime decarboxylation), which removes the -COONa group and replaces it with a hydrogen atom. Subsequent treatment with HCl(aq) protonates the phenoxide ion to form phenol. Thus, (B) is phenol.

The reaction of phenol with NaOH(aq) converts it back to sodium phenoxide, which is also labeled as (B) in the reaction scheme. This is a nucleophilic species.

The final step involves the reaction of sodium phenoxide with allyl bromide ($CH_2=CH-CH_2Br$). This is a Williamson ether synthesis where the phenoxide oxygen acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of the allyl bromide, displacing the bromide ion. This results in the formation of allyl phenyl ether, which is $C_6H_5-O-CH_2-CH=CH_2$.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound $[\mathrm{A}]\left(\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}\right)$, on reaction with conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ at $443 \mathrm{~K}$ gives $[\mathrm{B}]$ as one of the products. Compound [B] undergoes further reaction with $\mathrm{O}_3$ and $\mathrm{Zn} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ to give Propanone and Ethanal as products. Identify compound [A]
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of compound [A] is $C_5H_{12}O$, which corresponds to a saturated alcohol or ether. Since it reacts with conc. $H_2SO_4$ at $443 K$ to form an alkene [B], [A] is an alcohol.

The reaction of [B] with $O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$ (reductive ozonolysis) yields propanone ($CH_3COCH_3$) and ethanal ($CH_3CHO$).

The structure of the alkene [B] can be reconstructed by joining the carbonyl carbons of the products with a double bond. Propanone is $CH_3-C(=O)-CH_3$ and ethanal is $CH_3-CH=O$. Removing the oxygen atoms and joining the carbons gives $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$. This is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Compound [A] is an alcohol that undergoes dehydration to form 2-methylbut-2-ene. Among the given options, 3-methylbutan-2-ol ($CH_3-CH(OH)-CH(CH_3)_2$) can undergo dehydration via a carbocation rearrangement or direct elimination to form 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product according to Zaitsev's rule.

Specifically, 3-methylbutan-2-ol dehydrates to form 2-methylbut-2-ene as the most stable alkene product.

Answer: 3-Methylbutan-2-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: Primary alcohols are very easily oxidised to aldehydes, which are oxidised to acids with same number of C-atoms.
Secondary alcohols are very easily oxidised to ketones, which are oxidised to acids with same number of C-atoms.
Secondary alcohols are easily oxidised to ketones, which are oxidised to acids with lesser number of C-atoms.
Secondary and tertiary alcohols on oxidation form acids with lesser number of C-atoms.
questions.solution:
Primary alcohols are easily oxidised to aldehydes and then to acid, both containing the same number of carbon atoms, while secondary alcohols are easily oxidised to ketones with same number of carbon atoms, but ketone oxidised to carboxylic acid containing lesser number of carbon atoms than original alcohol.
Thus all alcohols on oxidation finally give acids but acids obtained from $2^{\circ}$ and $3^{\circ}$ alcohols contain less C-atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the starting compound from the following data:
$\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{14} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{X})$ on reaction with $\mathrm{HI}$ yields a haloalkane (A) and an alcohol (B). Compound (A) on reaction with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ gives an alcohol (C). Compounds (B) and (C) on reaction with $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ in anhydrous medium yields Butanone and Ethanal respectively.
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of compound (X) is $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{14} \mathrm{O}$, which corresponds to an ether. The reaction of ether (X) with $\mathrm{HI}$ produces a haloalkane (A) and an alcohol (B).

Compound (B) on oxidation with $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ yields Butanone. Since Butanone is a ketone, (B) must be a secondary alcohol, specifically Butan-2-ol ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH(OH)CH}_3$).

Compound (A) is a haloalkane derived from the other part of the ether. Reaction of (A) with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ yields alcohol (C). Alcohol (C) on oxidation with $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ yields Ethanal. Since Ethanal is an aldehyde, (C) must be a primary alcohol, specifically Ethanol ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$).

Therefore, the haloalkane (A) must be Ethyl iodide ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{I}$).

Combining the fragments (B) and (A) to form the original ether (X), we have $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH(OCH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{)CH}_3$. This structure is 2-ethoxybutane.

Answer: 2-Ethoxybutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: $\mathrm{m}$ - Cresol is a weaker acid than Phenol.
Acetylation of Salicylic acid produces 2-Acetoxybenzoic acid.
Phenol on heating with Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ yields sulphanilic acid.
Acidic nature of Phenol is due to -I effect of oxygen of the hydroxyl group.
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: m-Cresol has a $-CH_3$ group ($+I$ effect) which destabilizes the phenoxide ion → weaker acid than phenol.

(2) Correct: Acetylation of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) with acetic anhydride gives 2-acetoxybenzoic acid (aspirin).

(3) Incorrect: Phenol on heating with conc. $H_2SO_4$ undergoes sulfonation to give phenol-2-sulfonic acid or phenol-4-sulfonic acid (depending on temperature), not sulphanilic acid. Sulphanilic acid is obtained by heating aniline with conc. $H_2SO_4$.

(4) Correct: The acidic nature of phenol is due to resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion (the $-I$ effect of oxygen also contributes).

Incorrect statement: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct order of increasing acidic strength of the following compounds.
questions.solution:
The acidic strength of alcohols depends on the stability of the conjugate base (alkoxide ion) formed after the loss of a proton. The stability of the alkoxide ion is increased by the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) through the inductive effect (-I effect).

The compounds are $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, and $\mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$.

In $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, the ethyl group is electron-donating (+I effect), which destabilizes the alkoxide ion, making it the least acidic.

In $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$, the halogen atoms exert a strong -I effect. Fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine, so the -I effect of the $\mathrm{CF}_3$ group is stronger than that of the $\mathrm{CCl}_3$ group.

Stronger -I effect leads to greater stabilization of the negative charge on the oxygen atom, resulting in higher acidic strength. Therefore, the order of increasing acidic strength is $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH} \lt \mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH} \lt \mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}\lt \mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}\lt \mathrm{CF}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Product of the following reaction is

The reaction is intramolecular oxymercuration-demercuration on $\alpha$-terpineol.

$Hg(OAc)_2$ activates the double bond forming a mercurinium ion intermediate. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: Secondary alcohols are very easily oxidised to ketones, which are oxidised to acids with same number of C-atoms.
Secondary alcohols are easily oxidised to ketones, which are oxidised to acids with lesser number of $\mathrm{C}$-atoms.
Primary alcohols are very easily oxidised to aldehydes, which are oxidised to acids with same number of C-atoms.
Secondary and tertiary alcohols on oxidation form acids with lesser number of C-atoms.
questions.solution:
Primary alcohols are oxidized to aldehydes and then to carboxylic acids containing the same number of carbon atoms. This is a standard reaction sequence.

Secondary alcohols are oxidized to ketones. Further oxidation of ketones involves the cleavage of carbon-carbon bonds, which results in the formation of carboxylic acids with a lesser number of carbon atoms than the original alcohol.

Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation under normal conditions, but under vigorous conditions, they undergo carbon-carbon bond cleavage to form a mixture of acids with a lesser number of carbon atoms.

questions.q: In Friedal-Crafts alkylation reaction of phenol with chloromethane, the product formed will be
questions.solution:
Phenol is an electron-rich aromatic compound due to the presence of the hydroxyl group, which is strongly activating and ortho/para-directing.

Friedel-Crafts alkylation involves the reaction of an aromatic ring with an alkyl halide in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst like $AlCl_{3}$.

However, phenol reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst to form a phenoxide-aluminum complex. This complex deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution and makes the reaction difficult.

Despite this, under specific conditions, the electrophilic substitution occurs at the ortho and para positions due to the directing effect of the $-OH$ group.

Consequently, the reaction of phenol with chloromethane in the presence of a catalyst yields a mixture of ortho-cresol and para-cresol.

Answer: mixture of $o$-and $p$-cresol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a false statement?
options: Methoxymethane has higher boiling point than ethanol.
Alcohols are more soluble is water than hydracarbons of comparable molecular mass.
ortho-and para-nitrophenols are more acidic than phenols.
Phenol is more acidic than alcohol.
questions.solution:
Ethanol ($C_{2}H_{5}OH$) exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding due to the presence of the polar -OH group, which leads to a significantly higher boiling point compared to methoxymethane ($CH_{3}OCH_{3}$), which is an ether and lacks such hydrogen bonding. Therefore, the statement that methoxymethane has a higher boiling point than ethanol is false.

Alcohols are capable of forming hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making them more soluble in water than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass, which are non-polar. This statement is true.

The nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) is an electron-withdrawing group that stabilizes the phenoxide ion through both inductive and resonance effects. This stabilization increases the acidity of ortho- and para-nitrophenols compared to phenol. This statement is true.

Phenol is more acidic than alcohols because the phenoxide ion formed after the loss of a proton is resonance-stabilized by the benzene ring, whereas the alkoxide ion formed from an alcohol is not stabilized by resonance. This statement is true.

Answer: Methoxymethane has higher boiling point than ethanol.
